selection.name: C08 — Inspect AI
selection.role: Provisional semantic evaluation runner. Its documented sample records, partial failed logs and score history best match the failure-preserving evidence requirement. Agents can invoke its CLI; independent labels and uncertainty handling must come from the evaluation protocol.
selection.install_command:
git clone https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai.git
cd inspect_ai
git checkout c05398d897affcb85bd4cb9d10a7c03e1779a18e
uv sync --extra dev
selection.install_source: Pinned upstream README documents cloning and uv sync --extra dev; checkout adds the verified source pin. Requires Git, uv and Python >=3.10.

basis.shows: Supported source installation and evaluation CLI.
Dataset targets, heuristic and model grading, custom scorers, multiple scorers and rescoring.
Per-sample inputs, outputs, targets and scores; errors and tracebacks; readable partial failed logs; score edits retaining author, reason and history.
Default-branch commit on 2026-10-02 UTC, within 90 days.
Current-head Python 3.10 and 3.11 tests succeeded; slow tests were skipped. These are upstream CI observations, not target-host or semantic-accuracy measurements.
Unarchived; 368 open issues/PRs. Backlog size does not establish responsiveness.
Returned 404; a GitHub latest release was not found. PyPI release currency remains unverified, so the recommendation pins source.

The repository is unarchived, and its README explicitly deprecates it. [Commit API](https://api.github.com/repos/openai/skills/commits?per_page=1), [pinned README](https://github.com/openai/skills/blob/49f948faa9258a0c61caceaf225e179651397431/README.md).

layers.deciding_comparison: Inspect AI versus Promptfoo on the new WSL2 host, followed by macOS arm64. Freeze fresh task cases, rubrics and independently collected human labels before running either arm. Replay identical Claude Code/Codex outputs, preserving both reviewers' labels and unresolved disagreements. Keep the existing eight cases diagnostic-only. Include a safe, deliberately incorrect advice fixture as the negative control. Compare false approvals, correct rejection, uncertain outcomes, label agreement, and recovery of original failed/partial attempts after retries or interruption. Require case IDs, raw outputs, verifier results, judge reasons and immutable failure artifacts. Record clean-install success, latency and resource use. The present selection favors documented capability fit; it does not claim measured semantic superiority.
evidence_gaps: Evidence was collected October 1 EDT / October 2 UTC. No clean installation, target-host trial or fresh independently labeled comparison was performed.

CI observations concern the inspected default-branch commits, not proof that the selected release tags pass the same checks. Job conclusions were verified; full test logs and benchmark measurements were not independently reproduced.
WSL2 fit is inferred from Ubuntu/Linux support. Harbor requires functioning Docker integration; macOS arm64 task-image compatibility and Inspect/Inspector runtime behavior still need direct checks.
The selected frameworks do not require a GPU. No RTX 4090 speedup or local-model compatibility was measured; local runner/storage support does not imply offline model access.

Independent labeling and retention of uncertain disagreements are evaluation-protocol requirements. Playwright's README example traces the first retry, which alone does not prove retention of the initial failed attempt.
Issue response times and closure rates were not measured. Open-issue/PR counts were recorded as maintenance context, without treating them as quality rankings.

Astra/Max review was triggered by conflicting ShellCheck Apple Silicon documentation. Acceptance: the release API's official Darwin aarch64 asset overrides the outdated negative README sentence; native macOS execution remains unverified.

Budget used: 30 GitHub API requests, two web searches and zero successful page fetches. The mandated ctx_fetch_and_index route was blocked with 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never'; upstream files were read through GitHub API snapshots instead, so the requested page-fetch workflow could not be completed.
